task.description: Classify iris flowers into three species from sepal and petal measurements.

warnings: Small dataset (150 rows): CV standard errors will be wide relative to differences between models.

idea.title: Baseline: standardised logistic regression
idea.rationale: Start from the unmodified starter solution so every later change is measured against a known reference.

idea.title: Weaken L2 regularisation (C=1 → 10)
idea.rationale: Profile shows near-separable classes; the default penalty keeps predicted probabilities soft, which log-loss punishes.

reason: Paired t-test over 10 folds p=0.004; gain 0.0312 ≥ 0.5×SE (0.0051); select improved 0.1042 → 0.0779.

idea.title: Switch to HistGradientBoosting
idea.rationale: Trees capture interactions without feature engineering; worth checking a different family early.

reason: Worse than best (0.1418 vs 0.0812); 150 rows is too few for boosted trees to calibrate.

idea.title: Add petal area and petal length/width ratio
idea.rationale: Versicolor/virginica overlap along single petal axes; their product and ratio separate them more cleanly.

reason: Paired t-test p=0.071; gain 0.0069 ≥ 0.5×SE (0.0046); select improved 0.0779 → 0.0716.

idea.title: RBF-kernel SVM with Platt scaling
idea.rationale: A smooth non-linear boundary might fit the curved versicolor/virginica border better than a linear model.

reason: Not better than best (0.0791 vs 0.0743); Platt scaling adds variance on small folds.

idea.title: Push regularisation further (C=10 → 30)
idea.rationale: The C=10 step helped a lot; check whether the curve keeps going.

reason: Gain 0.0025 < 0.5×SE (0.0047), p=0.21 — indistinguishable from noise; select did not improve (0.0721 vs 0.0716).

idea.title: Drop sepal.width and the ratio feature
idea.rationale: sepal.width has the weakest class separation and the ratio is redundant with petal area; fewer inputs, same signal.

reason: Gain 0.0002 is within noise, but the pipeline uses one fewer raw input and one fewer derived feature and fits faster (0.039 s → 0.031 s); select did not get worse (0.0716 → 0.0688) — kept by the simplicity rule.

idea.title: Soft-voting ensemble: LR + SVC + kNN
idea.rationale: Blending three different families often squeezes out the last gains on tabular data.

idea.title: Random forest on the reduced feature set
idea.rationale: Bagged trees are robust on small data and need little tuning; a different family to rule out a local optimum.

idea.title: Distance-weighted kNN (k=11)
idea.rationale: Iris clusters are compact in scaled petal space; a local method may calibrate well.
